findings.F1: The book loses by being short almost all the time against coins that rise. It was short on 95.8 % of bars with a mean allocation of -0.78, and it lost 0.42 bps per bar: -0.47 bps came from the coins' own rise and only +0.05 bps from timing. It closed 8287 short trades with a mean of -5.7 % before fees. Its forecast is non-zero on any negative 24-hour return, so 202702 bars were active.
findings.F2: The book's result is a mirror of the coin's. It gained in the windows where the coins fell (w14: book +0.45 % a day, coin -0.43 %; w7: +0.30 % against -0.47 %). It lost in the windows where they rose (w11: -0.55 % against +1.26 %; w21: -0.74 % against +0.57 %). It lost on all 6 coins, from -0.08 % to -0.22 % a day.
findings.F3: Over the 5-day horizon there is no continuation after a large 24-hour drop.
findings.F4: Over the next day a large 24-hour drop is followed by a rebound, and the rebound grows with the drop.
findings.F5: The rebound is concentrated in coins standing 30 % or more below their 30-day high.
findings.F6: In coins 30 % or more below their 30-day high, a 24-hour rise of more than 1 times the 30-day average daily move is followed by a fall the next day: strength -0.26, t -3.5, 279 cases, unusual move -1.3 %.
findings.F7: The continuation of large drops appears only around 10 days, after the rebound.

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour return, read at an hourly close, is a drop of several times its 30-day average absolute daily return, the price rises over the next 1 day by more than the coin's usual 1-day move. The larger the drop in those multiples, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader should refuse to short a fresh hourly plunge and instead treat it as a reason to buy for a day, because the move that follows is a rebound several times the cost of a trade.
ideas.name: hourly plunge next-day rebound

ideas.idea: While a coin stands far below its 30-day high, the larger its 24-hour drop in multiples of its 30-day average absolute daily return, the larger its rise over the next 3 days. The deeper the coin stands below that high, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader buying plunges should do so mainly in coins already deep below their recent high, where the rebound is largest and covers the cost many times.
ideas.name: deep-drawdown plunge rebound

ideas.idea: While a coin stands far below its 30-day high, the larger its 24-hour rise in multiples of its 30-day average absolute daily return, the larger its fall over the next 1 day.
ideas.consequence: A sharp bounce in a coin deep below its recent high is a reason to short it, or to refuse to buy it, for the following day.
ideas.name: deep-drawdown bounce fades
